newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila bourse exodus peaks with chief's quitting.
newsitem.headline: Manila bourse exodus peaks with chief's quitting.

text.p: Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) President Vitaliano Nanagas left his job after a spate of resignations by four senior executives early this week, an official said on Saturday.
Nanagas, who had been at the exchange for just over five months, could not be reached for comment but stock exchange chairman Wilson Sy told reporters he left because of differences with his staff.

"There were a lot of irreconcilable differences between the staff and the president. It is something we had to take action on because they were irreconcilable," Sy said after the bourse's annual general meeting at which Sy was elected chairman for a second one-year term.
Analysts said the absence of a president was bound to slow down the exchange's reforms process, but officials said the officers were able to handle day-to-day activities.
The bourse would appoint a committee to search for a new president, Sy said.
Sy did not expand on the issues which led to Nanagas's departure but other officials said some recent recruitments at very high salaries had upset older employees.
On Friday, Nanagas played down the resignations of senior officials, saying they had left for "greener pastures".
Earlier in the week, other key bourse officials, including the heads of the compliance and surveillance and listing departments, had resigned for reasons not yet clear.
Exchange officials said on Saturday they had asked former compliance chief Tomas Tuazon, who also resigned early this year, and the other officials who had quit to rejoin.
Market speculation was that the resignations came after intense rivalries within the bourse over tough reform measures to be implemented.
On Thursday, Nanagas told reporters the stock exchange had decided to stop investigating potential insider trading and price manipulation cases.
The Manila Times newspaper quoted him as saying the probe was halted because "it was taking much too long in terms of investigating and it was inconclusive".
Sy said Nanagas offered his resignation late on Friday and it was accepted by the brokers at Saturday's meeting.
"I had to accept (Nanagas' resignation) because it seemed like it was a choice between the exchange and the president at that time," he said.
Nanagas, a former president of state-owned Philippine Deposit Insurance Corp and an ex-Citibank executive, joined the Philippine Stock Exchange in October last year.
In the same month, Philippine Stock Exchange (PSE) members voted in favour of key reforms aimed at making the market more transparent and seat-holders more accountable.
